channel.description: Recent content in music-videos on Loud Legends

item.title: DEFTONES Return With New Album PRIVATE MUSIC And First Single 'MY MIND IS A MOUNTAIN'; VIDEO
item.description: Deftones are officially back. The California alt-metal band has announced their new album, private music, and dropped its lead single, “my mind is a mountain,” along with a brand-new music video (watch below).

item.title: SOL INVICTO, Featuring Members Of DEFTONES And CYPRESS HILL, Releases Visualizer For 21-Minute Track 'Initium'
item.description: After more than a decade locked away in a private fan archive, SOL INVICTO has finally released Initium, a 21-minute experimental track recorded in 2011 (watch it below).

item.title: LORNA SHORE Releases 'Unbreakable' Single and Music Video: 'It Will Never Break Us Down'
item.description: Lorna Shore has dropped a new single, “Unbreakable”, along with a fresh music video, giving fans another preview of their next album, I Feel The Everblack Festering Within Me.

item.title: HALESTORM Releases New Music Video for 'DARKNESS ALWAYS WINS': 'Evil Prevails And The Good Depart First'
item.description: Halestorm has unveiled a new official video for “Darkness Always Wins,” the band’s first release of 2025 (watch it below). Directed by DJay Brawner and produced by Dave Cobb, the song builds slowly with a cinematic tone and sits firmly in the band’s hard rock catalog.

item.title: HOLLYWOOD UNDEAD Releases Emotional New Single 'SAVIOR': 'We Can’t Wait For You To Hear It'
item.description: Rock group Hollywood Undead has dropped a new single titled “Savior” (watch it below), offering fans a more personal and emotional look at the band’s sound. The track is out now through Sumerian Records.

item.title: The Lemonheads Drop New Single “In The Margin,” Share Details on First Album in Nearly 20 Years
item.description: After years of writing, drifting, and starting over, Evan Dando is back. The Lemonheads are set to release their first studio album in almost two decades, titled Love Chant, arriving October 24 via Fire Records.

item.title: Watch FEMME FATALE's New Video for 'Living Like There's No Tomorrow'
item.description: Femme Fatale, the rock band led by Lorraine Lewis, has returned with a new song called “Living Like There’s No Tomorrow” (watch it below). The track is now available through Cleopatra Records, and its official music video, directed by Vicente Cordero, is out now.

item.title: JACOBY SHADDIX Talks New PAPA ROACH Single With TOBY MORSE: 'It Felt Urgent, Honest, In Your Face'
item.description: Papa Roach is back with a new single, and they’ve brought along a longtime friend. The California rock band just released “Braindead” (watch it below), a high-energy track featuring Toby Morse, the lead singer of punk band H2O.

item.title: THREE DAYS GRACE Releases New Single 'DOMINATE' Ahead Of Upcoming Album
item.description: Three Days Grace has released a new single titled “Dominate” (watch the video at the end of the article), available today on all major streaming platforms. The track is part of the band’s upcoming eighth studio album, Alienation, scheduled for release on August 22, 2025, via RCA Records.

item.title: The BEST SONG to Introduce Someone to KORN, According to JONATHAN DAVIS
item.description: So you want to introduce someone to Korn. Good luck. You’ve got nearly three decades’ worth of dreadlocks, detuned guitars, and unresolved childhood trauma to work with.

item.title: When METALLICA Brought Back 'FRANTIC' Live And JAMES HETFIELD Roasted St. Anger
item.description: Back in 2021, Metallica briefly resurrected “Frantic”, the chaotic opener from their 2003 punching bag of an album, St. Anger. The band pulled the song out of retirement for a set at the Aftershock Festival on October 8 (watch the video below), years after it had mostly vanished from live shows following a few scattered appearances in 2019 and a much longer break since 2011.

item.title: FIT FOR A KING Announces New Album 'LONELY GOD', Shares Lead Single And Tracklist
item.description: Fit For A King have unveiled Lonely God, their eighth studio album, scheduled to arrive August 1, 2025 via Solid State Records. The announcement came with a music video (available at the end of this article) for the blistering title track, which showcases the band’s signature blend of gnarly riffs, guttural growls, heavy grooves, and a dash of industrial crunch.

item.title: REVOCATION Announces New Album 'New Gods, New Masters' With Guest Appearances From Cattle Decapitation, Gorguts, And More
item.description: Revocation will release their ninth studio album, New Gods, New Masters, on September 26 via Metal Blade Records. It’s their fifth record under the label and the follow-up to 2022’s Netherheaven.

item.title: JESSE LEACH Talks About KILLSWITCH ENGAGE's 'Aftermath': 'We All Have a Responsibility'
item.description: Killswitch Engage isn’t wasting time with metaphors or feel-good slogans in their latest single. The video for “Aftermath” just dropped, and it doesn’t sugarcoat a thing. If you were expecting a fun, breakdown-heavy anthem about “staying strong,” keep scrolling.

item.title: Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" Surpasses 2 Billion YouTube Views
item.description: Nirvana’s “Smells Like Teen Spirit” has now passed the 2-billion view mark on YouTube. After first being uploaded in 2009, the video quietly amassed its first billion by 2019.

item.title: Motörhead Releases 'Leavin’ Here' Video From Recently Discovered 1976 Tapes
item.description: After nearly five decades of dust, decay, and general disregard, Motörhead has cracked open the time capsule no one saw coming. The band has just dropped a music video for “Leavin’ Here”, a snarling slab of rock that also happens to be one of the oldest recordings from the Lemmy–Eddie Clarke–Phil Taylor era.

item.title: KILLSWITCH ENGAGE Shares Music Video For 'Collusion' Single From 'This Consequence' Album
item.description: Killswitch Engage is back with This Consequence, their ninth studio album, and they’ve just unleashed a music video for the track “Collusion”, which, spoiler alert, is NOT about happy things.

item.title: Zakk Wylde’s Black Label Society Drops 'Lord Humungus'—New Single Out Now
item.description: you ever hear a song so ridiculously heavy it makes you wanna run through a wall—like, FULL Kool-Aid Man mode—except the wall is made of steel and your doctor is already tired of your bullshit?

item.title: Arch Enemy's Alissa White-Gluz Joins Savage Lands on New Single “Ruling Queen”
item.description: I knew a guy once—swore on his mother’s grave that trees could scream. Not metaphorically, not some poetic nonsense about deforestation being a “cry for help.” No, he meant it literally, said he heard it with his own ears—a deep, resonant moan every time an axe struck bark.

item.title: Arch Enemy Drops "Paper Tiger" Music Video and Reveals Blood Dynasty Tour Dates
item.description: Ok SO listen—Arch Enemy decided that the world needed to be LOUDER, and who are we to argue??? They dropped “Paper Tiger” and I swear to Odin’s beard it’s got that Judas Priest but also Arch Enemy but also maybe a bit of an angry chainsaw vibe.

item.title: Meshuggah Drops "Ligature Marks" Music Video Alongside "Immutable - The Indelible Edition" Announcement
item.description: Yep, MESHUGGAH is back to make your speakers beg for mercy—again. Not just playing their usual brand of mind-melting, time-signature-abusing, existential-crisis-inducing metal—oh no, they’ve decided to remaster their already ridiculous 2022 album Immutable and slap on a shiny new title: “Immutable - The Indelible Edition” (because clearly, “Immutable” wasn’t immutable enough).

item.title: SPIRITBOX Releases "No Loss, No Love" Ahead of "Tsunami Sea" Album Drop; VIDEO
item.description: SPIRITBOX did what now? Dropped a new single? No Loss, No Love? A chaotic, genre-hopping, existential crisis in song form? Yeah, that checks out. This band is out here treating musical boundaries like a cheap piñata, just smashing them apart, stuffing the remains with eerie atmospherics and whatever the hell Courtney LaPlante feels like doing with her voice that day.

item.title: Stray From The Path Releases “Kubrick Stare” – A New Single Under SharpTone Records; VIDEO
item.description: Stray From The Path is back. And they’re bringing paranoia with them. Their latest single, “Kubrick Stare”, just dropped (February 5, 2025, mark it) with a music video that’s—well, unsettling, in the best way.

item.title: Watch: Marty Friedman Drops Visualizer for “A Prayer” From Drama
item.description: Marty Friedman, the once-and-forever legendary (but now solo and doing his thing) former MEGADETH guitarist, just threw a visualizer our way for his track “A Prayer.” You know, that song from his album Drama?

item.title: Watch: BREAKING BENJAMIN Releases Lyric Video for 'Awaken'
item.description: BREAKING BENJAMIN, the multi-platinum hard rock juggernaut, just released a lyric video for their latest single, “Awaken”. If you’re curious, the video is already floating around the internet—feel free to hunt it down.

item.title: The Surprise You Missed in Korn’s 1997 Track "A.D.I.D.A.S."
item.description: Ever really listened to the breakdown in Korn’s 1997 track “A.D.I.D.A.S.”? And I mean actually listened—ears glued to every sound, every tiny layer. There’s a surprise in there you probably missed.

item.title: Watch: DREAM THEATER Releases 'Night Terror' Video Ahead of 'Parasomnia' Album
item.description: February 7, 2025, marks the arrival of DREAM THEATER’s sixteenth album, “Parasomnia,” via InsideOut Music. This time, they’ve reunited with their prodigal son, drummer Mike Portnoy, whose last contribution to the band dates back to 2009’s “Black Clouds & Silver Linings.

item.title: Shavo Odadjian’s Seven Hours After Violet Drops New Single "Cry"; VIDEO
item.description: Shavo Odadjian is back with his new project—SEVEN HOURS AFTER VIOLET—and they’ve just dropped the music video for their latest single, “Cry.” Far from being a System of a Down copycat, this track goes straight into anguish, longing, and all the good ol’ despair you’d expect from a song called “Cry.

item.title: Watch: Linkin Park Partners with Riot Games for League of Legends Anthem
item.description: Linkin Park is back, boys and girls. Again. This time, they’ve teamed up with Riot Games for “Heavy Is The Crown,” the official anthem for the League of Legends 2024 World Championship.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Drops Emotional New Track, "The Cave We Fear to Enter"; VIDEO
item.description: Looks like As I Lay Dying has decided to venture into metaphorical spelunking. Their latest single, “The Cave We Fear to Enter,” leans heavily into clean vocals and was born out of an idea from bassist and vocalist Ryan Neff.

item.title: Watch: As I Lay Dying Is Back: 'Burden' Released, Tour Announced
item.description: As I Lay Dying has returned with “Burden”, their first new single in five years, featuring their revamped lineup. The track introduces Ken Susi (ex-Unearth), Nick Pierce (ex-Unearth), and Ryan Neff (Miss May I), marking a new chapter for the band.

item.title: Linkin Park Releases "Friendly Fire" Featuring Chester Bennington
item.description: Art has a way of keeping artists alive, doesn’t it? Even when they’re gone, their work lingers on, creating an odd form of immortality. Linkin Park just gave fans a bittersweet reminder of that idea by releasing “Friendly Fire”, an unreleased track featuring the unmistakable vocals of the late Chester Bennington.

item.title: Korn's Brian Welch Introduces New Record Label XOVR Records; VIDEO
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist from Korn, has decided that making loud noises on stage wasn’t quite enough, so he’s now entering the record label world with his latest venture, XOVR Records (that’s “Crossover Records” for those who don’t speak in mysterious abbreviations).

item.title: Watch: Metallica Drops New “Too Far Gone?” Video with Tour Highlights
item.description: Metallica might’ve dropped 72 Seasons a mere five months back, but the internet reaction could’ve fooled anyone into thinking it’s been years since that release. One side hollered about “disastrous trash,” while the other shrugged, calling it “pretty decent.
